identity.name: Andy Miah
identity.title: Chair in Science Communication & Future Media
identity.tagline: Interdisciplinary research leader in AI ethics, creative technologies, and civic innovation

profile.core:
Professor Andy Miah is an internationally recognised interdisciplinary research leader with 18 years of Professorial experience spanning Arts & Humanities, Science & Engineering, and Health Sciences. His work examines the ethics of emerging technologies — from AI and biotechnology to immersive media, esports, and digital health — always with a commitment to societal impact and creative practice.

He is Chair in Science Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford, where he founded and directs The Science Communication Space, a cross-university platform integrating research, creative practice, and public engagement. He is Principal Investigator on a £4.5 million Innovate UK Accelerator mobilising over 250 Greater Manchester businesses into a CreaTech innovation ecosystem, and has served for six years on the Agora Committee of the Swiss National Science Foundation, overseeing approximately £18 million in interdisciplinary public engagement funding.

Andy has published over 250 works including 10 books, among them Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017) and Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004), with a forthcoming monograph under review at Oxford University Press. He has given over 450 invited talks in more than 50 countries, received the Josh Award for Science Communication from the Science and Industry Museum, Manchester, and is a member of the DCMS College of Experts. He is a Board Member of the British Esports Federation, Commission Member of the Global Esports Federation, and Marketing Manchester Ambassador.

variants.esports:
Professor Andy Miah is one of the UK's foremost academic authorities on esports, digital sport, and competitive gaming. He has been active in the esports sector for over a decade — as a researcher, governance board member, keynote speaker, and industry adviser — combining scholarly rigour with sustained practical engagement across the full breadth of the sector.

He organised the first dedicated esports research conference at a UK university (Salford, 2016), has served as Board Member of the British Esports Federation since 2019, Commission Member of the Global Esports Federation since 2020, and Commission Chair of the World Technology Games since 2025. He has presented at the UN ITU AI for Good programme on safe digital spaces through esports, keynoted the Global Esports Executive Summit (Busan, 2017), ESIC Global Esports Summits (London, 2022 and 2023), Peace and Sport International Forum (Monaco, 2019), and the Esports in Education Summit at BETT (2022, 2026).

His published work includes The Esports Question for the Olympic Movement (Journal of Olympic Studies, 2021), Esport in the Olympic and Paralympic Games (Routledge, 2020), and Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017) — which includes a sustained analysis of esports, digital spectatorship, and the transformation of competitive gaming. His £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator included a dedicated gametech and esports R&D strand connecting academic research with industry development across Greater Manchester.
variants.creative-manchester:
Professor Andy Miah is an interdisciplinary research leader with over 20 years embedded in the Greater Manchester creative and civic ecosystem. He has built and led major cross-sector platforms connecting universities, cultural institutions, industry, and policy — with a sustained commitment to creativity, ethics, and inclusive innovation.

At the University of Salford, he is Principal Investigator on a £4.5 million Innovate UK Accelerator that mobilised over 250 Greater Manchester SMEs into a CreaTech innovation ecosystem with MediaCity and Salford City Council, spanning gametech, esports, immersive experiences, and virtual production. He chairs the University's Engagement Forum, has led a decade-long partnership with Manchester Science Festival, and is appointed Marketing Manchester Ambassador. He works closely with GMCA, Factory International, Contact Theatre, Abandon Normal Devices, and FutureEverything, and facilitated the launch of the Diaspora Innovation Network with Aviva Studios in 2025.

His research spans all three of Creative Manchester's themes — Creative Industries & CreaTech, Creative and Civic Futures, and Creativity, Health and Wellbeing — and he has active collaborations with colleagues across the University of Manchester, including a joint bid to bring the British Science Festival to Manchester in 2027. He has contributed to two REF cycles focused on Impact, served on six years of the Swiss National Science Foundation's Agora Committee overseeing £18m in interdisciplinary public engagement, and holds appointments on the DCMS College of Experts and the World Technology Group.
variants.science-communication:
Professor Andy Miah is an award-winning science communicator and public intellectual whose career has been defined by making complex ideas in ethics, technology, and society accessible to diverse audiences across academia, media, policy, and the public.

He is Director of The Science Communication Space at the University of Salford — a cross-university platform integrating research, creative practice, and public engagement — and Academic Lead for the Manchester Science Festival partnership, now in its tenth year. He leads the FameLab North West Regional Hub and has co-led over 100 art-science collaborations at festivals including Cheltenham Science Festival, New Scientist Live, Edinburgh Science Festival, and Blue Dot. He has given over 450 invited talks in more than 50 countries, and received the Josh Award for Science Communication from the Science and Industry Museum, Manchester, in 2015.

For over six years he served on the Agora Committee of the Swiss National Science Foundation, overseeing approximately £18 million in science communication and public engagement funding across 200+ interdisciplinary projects. He is a regular broadcast commentator on BBC Newsnight, Sky News, and CNN, a columnist for The Conversation, and most recently appeared in Future Tense (Audible, 2025, with Richard Ayoade and Warwick Davis). He has published over 250 works and is a member of the DCMS College of Experts and Marketing Manchester Ambassador.
variants.ai-ethics:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading voice on AI ethics and emerging technologies, whose work bridges philosophy, policy, and creative practice to address the ethical and societal implications of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and digital futures.

He serves as a member of the UK Government's DCMS College of Experts, was Ethics Lead for the Greater Manchester AI Foundry (2020–2023), and sits on the Oversight Committee for the PROBABLE Futures project (£3.4m, RAi Keystone) on probabilistic AI in law enforcement. He led Task and Finish Groups on AI Research Policy and AI Teaching & Learning Strategy at the University of Salford, and advises the World Technology Group and Advisory Board. His Principal Investigator role on a £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator encompassed AI-adjacent technologies including immersive media, metaverse applications, and generative tools for creative industries.

His published work spans AI ethics, posthumanism, gene doping, nanotechnology, and digital futures — including over 250 publications and 10 books, a forthcoming monograph under review at Oxford University Press, and contributions to government select committee inquiries and international policy forums. He chairs the Metaverse Special Interest Group at Salford and has keynoted at the Government Office for Science, South by Southwest, the UN ITU AI for Good programme, and Edinburgh Science Festival on AI ethics, digital society, and the future of human-technology relations.
variants.bioethics:
Professor Andy Miah is a foundational figure in the bioethics of human enhancement, gene doping, and posthumanism, whose work has shaped academic, policy, and public debate on the ethical boundaries of biotechnology and emerging technology for over two decades.

His book Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004) remains a defining text in the field, drawing on philosophy, law, and sport science to examine gene doping and human enhancement. This was followed by The Medicalization of Cyberspace (Routledge, 2008, with Emma Rich), which examined the intersection of digital technology and health governance, and Drones (Emerald, 2020), which brought his ethical framework to bear on autonomous systems. He holds an MPhil in Medical Law and Ethics from the University of Glasgow and a PhD in Bioethics and Philosophy of Technology from De Montfort University, and was an International Visiting Scholar at The Hastings Center for Bioethics, New York.

He has presented evidence to Government Select Committees, keynoted at Harvard Law School, the European Parliament, the Royal Institution of Great Britain, and Wellcome Trust events, and has been a regular contributor to BBC, The Guardian, and Washington Post on human enhancement, genetic technologies, and the ethics of emerging biotechnology. He has published over 250 works across philosophy, bioethics, science and technology studies, and health sociology, and holds editorial board positions on NanoEthics (Springer) and Performance Enhancement and Health (Springer).
variants.digital-health:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading researcher in digital health technologies, examining how wearable devices, mobile health platforms, immersive media, and AI-driven systems are transforming healthcare, wellbeing, and the governance of bodies and health data.

His co-authored book The Medicalization of Cyberspace (Routledge, 2008) was among the first sustained academic analyses of digital health as a societal phenomenon. His Wellcome Trust-funded research (£130,000, with the University of Bath and University of Canberra) examined digital health technologies and young people, and his peer-reviewed articles in Health Sociology Review and Sociology of Health and Illness examine the equity implications of wearable and mobile health platforms. He has also written for The Conversation on AI and the NHS, mental healthcare in gaming environments, and the ethics of health data.

He has given keynotes at the Healthy City Design Congress and Digital Health Generation event at the Houses of Parliament, and was invited to address the MeCCSA conference on digital health and young people. His research connects digital health to broader questions of social responsibility, data ethics, and inclusive design — increasingly through the lens of AI and immersive technology, including work on VR interfaces for clinical practice developed as part of his Innovate UK Accelerator programme.
variants.olympic-studies:
Professor Andy Miah is an internationally recognised authority on the Olympic Games, sport governance, and the intersection of sport, media, and emerging technology. He co-founded the Culture @ the Olympics digital platform in 2001 — one of the first online resources dedicated to the cultural dimensions of the Olympic movement — and has conducted fieldwork at every Summer and Winter Olympics from Sydney 2000 to Paris 2024.

His books include The Olympics: The Basics (Routledge, 2012, with Beatriz Garcia) and Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017), which examines the digital transformation of sport including esports, fan engagement, and the future of mega-events. He has published on the ethics of human enhancement in sport, the role of non-accredited media at the Olympics, and the future of esports within the Olympic programme — including The Esports Question for the Olympic Movement (Journal of Olympic Studies, 2021). He mentored the IOC's Young Reporters Programme (2014) and has keynoted at the International Olympic Academy, Olympism in Action Forum (Buenos Aires, 2018), and Chinese Taipei Olympic Academy.

He has been funded by The British Academy (x2) and Carnegie Trust (x2) for Olympic research, and has advised the IOC and peace and sport organisations on the role of esports in the Olympic movement and sport diplomacy. He is a regular media commentator on the Olympics for BBC, The Guardian, and international broadcast outlets.
variants.platform-leadership:
Professor Andy Miah is an experienced interdisciplinary platform leader with a sustained track record of building and directing cross-sector research ecosystems that connect universities, cultural institutions, industry, and civic partners around shared strategic goals.

He founded and directed the Creative Futures Institute at the University of the West of Scotland (2011–2014), a cross-faculty interdisciplinary research unit, before establishing The Science Communication Space at the University of Salford — a platform integrating research, creative practice, and civic engagement across multiple schools and external partners. He chairs the University's Engagement Forum, has contributed to two REF Impact cycles, led Task and Finish Groups on AI Research Policy and AI Teaching & Learning Strategy, and advised on a £6.5m campus connectivity project. As Principal Investigator on a £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator, he built and managed a CreaTech innovation ecosystem mobilising 250+ Greater Manchester businesses, with a 2:1 co-investment leverage ratio.

For six years he served on the Agora Committee of the Swiss National Science Foundation, overseeing approximately £18 million in interdisciplinary public engagement funding across 200+ projects. He holds appointments as DCMS College of Experts member, Marketing Manchester Ambassador, Board Member of the British Esports Federation, Commission Member of the Global Esports Federation, and Commission Chair of the World Technology Games — reflecting the breadth of his strategic leadership across academic, civic, cultural, and industry sectors.
